title: Startup Exercise: what money can't solve (team, authority, learning) is what's most valuable
summary: Jason Cohen separates what money can fix (execution, ads, code, QA, runway) from what it can't (finding great people, authority, knowing what to build, learning). He argues exploration can't be bought while execution can, and shows how to use this when pitching investors or competing against better-funded rivals.

principles.text: Execution can be bought with money; exploration cannot. Money only accelerates once you know what to do.
principles.quote: Execution can be solved with money; exploration cannot.

principles.text: Great people are scarce and always have options, so money alone won't find them. Money helps only after you find the person.
principles.quote: If someone handed me a million dollars it wouldn't help me find an awesome person; they're just scarce.

principles.text: Most marketing can be bought (ads, campaigns, landing page tests, freemium), but authority-driven attention from blogging and social media cannot.
Concepts, behaviors, knowledge and process can't be bought. Money becomes an accelerant once you know how to learn quickly.
principles.quote: Concepts, behaviors, knowledge, and process cannot be fabricated with money, and possibly cannot even be accelerated.

principles.text: When raising money, name the unsolved problems before investors do and bring a clear plan. Without one, wait.
principles.quote: If you don't have a clear, plausible plan, don't raise money yet.

principles.text: Don't raise money before the core team is assembled, since cash can't fix a missing team.
principles.quote: Specifically, don't raise money if you haven't assembled the core team.
